newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexican rebel group declares truce until New Year.
newsitem.headline: Mexican rebel group declares truce until New Year.

text.p: Mexico's leftist Popular Revolutionary Army guerrillas declared a unilateral Christmas truce on Friday.
The group, which first appeared in June and mounted attacks in several states in August, said it would suspend "military harassment" operations until January 7.
Known as the EPR from its Spanish initials, the group said it was still prepared to repel any attacks by government forces, however.
At least 25 people have died in EPR attacks since it first appeared June 28 in the poor southern state of Guerrero.

Mexico's only other guerrilla group to have demonstrated any firepower, the Zapatista National Liberation Army, has been in peace talks with the government for more than a year and a half. Its January 1, 1994 uprising lasted only 12 days before a cease-fire was struck.
